stem: During a storage audit, 500 TB of archival data must move from an on-premises NAS to Amazon S3 over an existing network link on a recurring nightly schedule, and the goal is the lowest ongoing service fee for the transfer method itself.

choices.text: Deploy AWS Storage Gateway to keep serving the data indefinitely from a local cache
Set up AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints for the transfer
Use AWS DataSync on a recurring schedule for the transfer
Request a one-time AWS Data Transfer Terminal shipment for this dataset

rationale: AWS DataSync is billed per GB transferred with no appliance to run, and it can run on a recurring schedule over the existing network link, fitting both the recurring requirement and the lowest ongoing service fee. Storage Gateway is built for keeping an on-premises application running indefinitely against a local cache, not for a scheduled bulk migration job. Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS, and AS2 endpoints for external partners exchanging files, not a bulk NAS-to-S3 transfer job. AWS Data Transfer Terminal is a physical shipment path for datasets too large to move over the network in time, which does not fit a transfer that already has a usable network link.
